intervention.once: Frozen recovery_repeat once strategy, qualifications and continued shadow observation, with at most one actual queue bypass and one bypass per request/preemption episode.
intervention.gc_observation: Attach one passive gc.callbacks observer after warmup at the existing measurement observer boundary; remove only that callback during finally and dump gc-observation.json. Preserve existing GC enablement and thresholds. No forced collection or scheduling/model/parameter changes.

correctness_scope: Only CPU combined-source and CLI boundaries plus the probe own callback-lifecycle checks. Reuse existing lock, resource safety, workload, termination and native runtime paths.
source_basis: Frozen recovery_repeat runner and once policy plus passive gc_probe install()->(data, uninstall) at the existing post-warmup observer installation boundary.
primary_readout: GC intervals overlapping the three common host pauses, their generation and retained duration; pairing anomalies and pending callbacks; unchanged raw host/request metrics and actual output/copy work for diagnostic context. Interval overlap alone is not causal evidence or a measured speedup.

gc_observation.clock: time.perf_counter host clock; align against raw measurement origin/end without altering raw timestamps
gc_observation.retained_events: All generation-2 collections and paired events lasting at least 0.001 seconds; this is logging detail, not a scheduling threshold.
gc_observation.short_event_accounting: per_generation aggregates cover the entire installation window; short events without individual timestamps cannot be exactly cropped to the raw measurement interval.
gc_observation.lifecycle: Record installation/uninstallation host time, GC enablement and thresholds; pair start/stop callbacks, retain pairing anomalies and pending_at_uninstall.
gc_observation.causal_limit: Passive diagnostic only. GC overlap can support localization but does not establish the complete cause or net benefit of a GC policy change.
